name: page-long-subtitle
note: A subtitle that runs past `width=100`, so the description goes through `textwrap.shorten(subtitle, width=100, placeholder="...")` (core.py:703-705). It carries a `state-of-the-art` compound on purpose: CPython's `break_on_hyphens=True` splits ordinary words at hyphens too, and the truncation point can therefore land *inside* a hyphenated word, which a whitespace split would not do. This fixture is the integration — that `generate_metadata` really routes the subtitle through `shorten`, and that the second escaping pass runs over the shortened result. The truncation mechanics themselves are pinned word for word against CPython by the golden table in `crates/medium-doc/src/textwrap.rs`; there is deliberately no expected value here, because a second hand-maintained copy of what Python produces is a second thing that can be wrong.

post.title: A Post With A Long Subtitle

previewContent.subtitle: A subtitle that is long enough to be shortened, with a state-of-the-art detour and enough further words after it that the hundred column limit forces the placeholder to appear somewhere near the end of it.
